biggest_catch: Earnings are fully variable — most proposals win nothing — and Workana takes 20% of your first $300 with every new client.
catches: Commission is 20% on the first $300 earned with each new client, then 10% up to $3,000, then 5% — one-off gigs keep paying the top tier.
Optional paid benefit plans exist but are explicitly not mandatory to bid or work.
Most proposals lose; earnings depend entirely on winning client work.
Client-set budgets; Workana publishes no fixed freelancer pay range.
Disputes go through Workana arbitration; repeated breaches can suspend your account.

c1.evidence: Workana's own help center states: 'For creating a profile, creating a project and or sending proposals to the projects are free of charge.' and 'the client can publish his projects and find the freelancer who can best carry out his project' — a public project/proposal marketplace.

c2.evidence: Official terms publish no fixed freelancer pay range — pay is per project with a published tiered commission; framed as variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official flow: free approved profile, search jobs, send proposals, escrow-funded execution, client-released payment.

c4.evidence: Profile creation and proposal-sending are free; benefit plans are explicitly 'not mandatory' per the official article.

eligibility: Anyone who can create an account, pass Workana profile approval, and legally freelance; skills must match posted projects.
notes: Scenario: freelance bidding. Workana is a freelance bidding marketplace (LATAM-strong, global): clients publish projects, freelancers send proposals for free, and awarded work pays through escrow. Pay is per-project and variable — never guaranteed.
numeric_basis: payout: per-project, client-set budgets, no official range. time: free profile setup + approval + reading and submitting first proposals, est. 45-120 min active.

steps: Create a free Workana freelancer profile and get it approved.
Search client-posted projects in your area of expertise and send proposals (free; proposals use connections).
If hired, the client funds an escrow deposit before work starts.
Execute the work through the platform's chat and file sharing.
The client releases payment on approval; Workana applies its tiered commission (20%/10%/5% by client lifetime volume).
timing: Projects post continuously; escrow releases when the client approves the work.
